policy.raw_capture: The initiating failure is represented by this reviewed ledger entry over its immutable run evidence. Every later nonzero S1-13 PBS experiment exit writes an immutable raw JSON record below that run's failures directory.
policy.reviewed_analysis: Every failed experiment must be added to this ledger with the failure, evidence-backed cause, and expected solution.
policy.resubmission_gate: No later experiment may be submitted until the preceding failure has a reviewed ledger entry and its proposed correction has been statically reviewed.

failures.workload: five-node four-learner plus CPU-only syncer long-run preflight smoke

failure.summary: The syncer exhausted the frozen 1200-second active-runtime budget before reaching the required long-smoke progress.
failure.exception: TimeoutError: frozen active runtime budget expired

cause.summary: The filesystem control/data path performed redundant whole-fragment CPU and storage work, so the syncer could not consume the available proposals at the required cadence.
direct_evidence: env/tracejob.txt records exit status 1 after 00:21:11 walltime.
stderr/mpirun.log records the frozen active-runtime TimeoutError.
logs/syncer.jsonl contains exactly 140 contiguous fragment updates, 35 per fragment, with median merge/update latency 1.758271361 seconds.
All four learner role records reach 3000 local steps and together process 24576000 input tokens, so learner training completion was not the terminal failure.
implementation_defects_found: The S_max=0 global-state encoding stored the current parameter payload twice: once as current parameters and again as the newest retained base.
Syncer readiness rehashed every cached 154-170 MB proposal payload on repeated polls even though proposal construction and decoding had already validated immutable bytes.
Learner publication constructed proposal identities and hashes on the training thread instead of the per-fragment publisher worker.
POSIX publication verification allocated and read a second full payload instead of comparing the committed payload in bounded chunks.
cause.confidence: high that these defects materially caused the throughput shortfall; the corrected throughput remains to be validated on a reduced compute run

changes: Encode the current retained base as an explicit alias of current parameters and store only older retained bases.
Validate proposal payload identity once at the immutable protocol boundary and stop rehashing unchanged cached proposals during readiness polling.
Move proposal materialization and hashing to the fragment publisher worker while keeping GPU-to-CPU snapshot capture at the safe boundary.
Verify POSIX payload publication with bounded chunk comparison rather than a second full allocation.
Use exact bound-record reads so adoption and atomic commit consume the payload named by the already validated visibility record.
validation_before_next_full_experiment: Complete the production and auxiliary code review and correct all findings.
Pass static lint and type checks and the complete Stage 1 test suite on a compute node.
Run the smallest admissible runtime reproduction and confirm payload sizes, hashing counts, readiness cadence, and global-cycle throughput before another five- or nine-node run.

failures.workload: one-node identity-bound static and complete Stage 1 targeted regression

failure.summary: The identity-bound targeted regression failed the complete Stage 1 pytest gate after all static gates passed.

observed_progress.pyright: pass with zero errors and warnings

cause.summary: The pre-runtime review changes were statically valid but seven regression expectations or dependent consumers were not updated consistently.
root_causes: Two corruption tests rewrote visibility JSON with noncanonical formatting, so the new canonical storage boundary correctly rejected the record before the tests reached their intended deeper identity mismatch.
The selective-shard test expected the underlying LearnerAssetError even though PackedTokenShard deliberately translates asset failures to LearnerError.

Sorting tied-parameter aliases made lm_head.weight the recorded owner_name; PyTorch remove_duplicate=True exposes only transformer.wte.weight for GPT-2, so two real tied-weight group builders could not resolve the canonical parameter.
The readiness stress validator omitted the newly identity-bearing logical_syncer_id field from its exact frozen-selection schema.
A static package test searched for a single-line source literal that the formatter had split across lines.
cause.scope: No learner/syncer runtime reproduction was launched. The failure occurred entirely inside the authorized one-node targeted regression.

changes: Make visibility-corruption fixtures emit canonical record bytes before asserting the intended semantic mismatch.
Assert the PackedTokenShard public LearnerError boundary for a corrupted selected shard.
Choose a stable owner alias below the logical owner path and resolve tied parameters through the complete alias view rather than remove_duplicate=True.
Add and validate logical_syncer_id in the readiness stress schema and selection identity.
Make the package source assertion insensitive to formatting-only line breaks.
Remove the syncer's unbounded in-memory update and inventory histories; retain append-only evidence in the durable structured log and keep only scalar counts in the live role state.
Keep pre-authorization and output-reuse failures outside the rejected experiment root, and bind failure capture to the experiment root only after exclusive authorization succeeds.

static_validation.pyright: pass with zero errors and warnings
static_validation.bash_syntax: pass for every active S1-13 PBS script and failure helper

validation_before_next_experiment: Pass compileall, Ruff, Pyright, diff checks, and all S1-13 PBS Bash syntax checks again.
Return the reviewed failure and exact correction diff to the same Checker for retry authorization.
Use a new identity-bound commit and verified nonexistent output root for any single targeted retry.
